report.title: Anthropic ships 10 Claude agent templates for financial services
report.summary: Ten ready-to-run agent templates for pitchbooks, KYC screening, GL reconciliation, and month-end close — each deployable as a Claude Cowork plugin or a fully autonomous Managed Agent in days, not months. Claude also gets full Microsoft 365 integration (Excel, PowerPoint, Word GA; Outlook beta) and new data connectors including Moody's full platform as a native app.

report.title: OpenAI makes GPT-5.5 Instant the default ChatGPT model
report.summary: GPT-5.5 Instant replaced GPT-5.3 Instant as the ChatGPT default on May 5, with a stated focus on cutting hallucinations in law, medicine, and finance while keeping latency low. Plus and Pro users on web get it first; free and enterprise tiers follow in coming weeks.

report.title: AWS lets AI agents operate WorkSpaces virtual desktops with assigned identities
report.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now previews support for agents to log into and operate WorkSpaces VMs under unique non-human identities, making agent actions auditable and distinct from human actions. Practical for enterprises that need agents inside existing desktop workflows rather than rebuilding everything around APIs.

report.title: Anthropic and FIS deploy AML investigation agent at BMO and Amalgamated Bank
report.summary: FIS launched a financial-crimes AI agent co-built with Anthropic's forward-deployed engineers, targeting anti-money laundering workflows — compressing multi-hour investigations to minutes by assembling evidence across bank systems and surfacing high-risk cases with full audit trails. BMO and Amalgamated Bank are the first two live deployments.

report.title: Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI agree to US pre-release AI model reviews
report.summary: The three labs agreed to let the Commerce Department's AI safety unit review new frontier models before public release, focusing on capabilities and national security risks. No veto power for the government, but it marks pre-release evaluation becoming a standard step in the frontier model release cycle.

report.title: Etsy launches native ChatGPT app for conversational shopping
report.summary: Etsy shipped a native app inside ChatGPT aimed at conversational product discovery, joining a growing set of retail integrations on the OpenAI platform. No API details yet — announced product, public availability still unclear.

report.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore expands to GovCloud (US-West)
report.summary: AgentCore — runtime, identity, gateway, policy, observability, and browser tools — is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-West), opening the production agent platform to US federal and defense workloads with existing FedRAMP/ITAR requirements.

learn.name: OpenAI Symphony
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-source spec that turns your Linear board into an always-on Codex agent farm.

detail.whatItDoes:
Symphony is an orchestration layer that watches a Linear project board and assigns a dedicated Codex agent workspace to every open ticket. Agents run continuously — restarting on crash, rebasing on conflict, monitoring CI — and hand off a pull request for human review. Behavior per repo is configured via a WORKFLOW.md file, so each project shapes what its agents do.

The reference implementation is written in Elixir under the Apache 2.0 license and built on top of the Codex App Server. Access to the Linear API token is kept out of subagent containers via a dynamic linear_graphql tool call rather than direct token exposure — a deliberate security tradeoff you should understand before deploying.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineering teams already running OpenAI Codex who have hit the context-switching ceiling of managing 3–5 concurrent agent sessions. Works best in repositories that have been hardened for agent use: good test coverage, clear ticket scope, and a CI gate that Codex can read. Solo developers running a Linear workspace will also benefit, though the payoff scales with ticket volume.
pros: 500% internal PR throughput lift at OpenAI in three weeks — a credible real-world benchmark
Language-agnostic spec; the Elixir reference impl is a starting point, not a requirement
WORKFLOW.md per repo means each project gets custom agent behavior without forking the orchestrator
Apache 2.0 license — no usage fees or lock-in
cons: OpenAI treats Symphony as a reference implementation, not a maintained product — you own the fork
Requires a well-structured repo with automated tests; poorly specified tickets produce poor output
Codex App Server is still evolving rapidly; Symphony will need updates as the API changes
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node 20+ (for Codex CLI)
- Elixir 1.16+ and Erlang/OTP 26+ (for the reference orchestrator)
- A Linear workspace with API access
- OpenAI API key with Codex access
- A repo that already runs CI (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, etc.)

## Step 1 — Install the Codex CLI

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex
codex --version
```

## Step 2 — Clone and configure Symphony

```bash
git clone https://github.com/openai/symphony
cd symphony
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env`:

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
LINEAR_API_KEY=lin_api_...
LINEAR_TEAM_ID=your-team-id
CODEX_APP_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:8080
```

## Step 3 — Add WORKFLOW.md to your target repo

```markdown
# WORKFLOW

## Scope
Fix bugs and implement features described in the linked Linear issue.

## Definition of done
- All existing tests pass
- New tests cover the changed code paths
- PR description summarizes the change in plain English

## Off-limits
Do not modify migration files or secrets. Escalate to a human if the ticket 
requires architecture decisions.
```

## Step 4 — Start the Codex App Server

```bash
codex app-server --port 8080
```

## Step 5 — Start Symphony

```bash
mix deps.get
mix run --no-halt
```

Symphony will now poll your Linear board, spawn one Codex agent workspace per open ticket in the configured state, and push PRs when CI passes.

## Gotcha
The `--full-auto` flag in Codex is deprecated. Symphony uses explicit permission profiles instead. If you see warnings about `--full-auto`, update to the latest Codex CLI and set `trust_level = "sandboxed"` in your `codex.toml`.

learn.name: DeerFlow 2.0
learn.oneLineDescription: ByteDance's open-source super-agent harness: spawn parallel sub-agents, memory, sandboxes — batteries included.

detail.whatItDoes:
DeerFlow 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite of ByteDance's Deep Research framework — it shares no code with v1. The lead agent decomposes tasks and spawns sub-agents on the fly, each with its own scoped context, tools, and termination conditions. Sub-agents run in parallel and report structured results back for synthesis. Tasks that take minutes to hours — multi-source research reports, code generation pipelines, dashboard creation — are the design target.

Built on LangGraph and LangChain, it ships with a filesystem, persistent memory, skill marketplace, sandbox-aware execution, and a message gateway for Slack, Telegram, and other channels. It is model-agnostic and works with any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint, though it performs best with models that have 100k+ context windows and strong tool-use.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers and researchers who need to run long-horizon agentic tasks (deep research, competitive analysis, multi-step data pipelines) and want a self-hosted harness rather than a cloud agent product. Also useful for teams building Claude Code or Codex integrations — DeerFlow ships a native /claude-to-deerflow Claude Code skill out of the box. Data engineers automating content workflows or report generation will find the skill system and MCP server support practical.
pros: Hit #1 on GitHub Trending on launch day (Feb 28 2026) — large community and active plugin ecosystem
Native Claude Code integration via /claude-to-deerflow skill command
MCP server support with OAuth token flows (client_credentials, refresh_token)
Model-agnostic: swap DeepSeek v3.2, Doubao, Kimi, or any OpenAI-compatible model via config.yaml
cons: v2 is a full rewrite — v1 skills and configs do not migrate; check the 1.x branch if you need the old framework
Complex multi-agent setups can burn tokens quickly; no built-in spend guardrails in the default config
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.11+
- `uv` (recommended) or `pip`
- Docker (optional, for sandboxed execution)
- An LLM API key (OpenAI, DeepSeek, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)

## Step 1 — Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow
cd deer-flow
uv sync
```

Or with pip:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Step 2 — Configure models

```bash
cp config.yaml.example config.yaml
```

Edit `config.yaml`:

```yaml
models:
  - name: primary
    display_name: GPT-5.5
    use: langchain_openai:ChatOpenAI
    model: gpt-5.5
    api_key: $OPENAI_API_KEY

  - name: fast
    display_name: DeepSeek v3.2
    use: langchain_openai:ChatOpenAI
    model: deepseek-chat
    base_url: https://api.deepseek.com/v1
    api_key: $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
```

## Step 3 — Set environment variables

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
export DEERFLOW_URL=http://localhost:2026
```

## Step 4 — Start DeerFlow

```bash
make dev
```

DeerFlow starts on `http://localhost:2026` by default.

## Step 5 — Run a research task

```python
import httpx

response = httpx.post(
    "http://localhost:2026/api/task",
    json={
        "task": "Research the top 5 vector database options for production RAG pipelines. Compare latency, cost, and managed offering availability. Produce a Markdown report.",
        "mode": "pro"  # Options: flash, standard, pro, ultra
    }
)
print(response.json())
```

## Gotcha
`make dev` requires a valid `config.yaml` before it starts — it will fail silently if the file is missing or malformed. Run `make config` first if you haven't copied the example file. The sandbox mode (Docker) adds startup latency; use `local` mode for quick iteration.

learn.name: Claude Managed Agents
learn.oneLineDescription: Anthropic's hosted long-horizon agent runtime with durable sessions, sandboxes, and task budgets.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Managed Agents is a public-beta service on the Claude Platform that provides a hosted runtime for long-running agentic tasks. It exposes stable interfaces for sessions, harnesses, and sandboxes — keeping state alive across multi-step work without developers managing the infrastructure. Task budgets (also in public beta) let you cap token spend per run, which matters when a single agent workflow might run for hours.

The financial-services agent templates shipped May 5 use Managed Agents as the delivery mechanism: each template is a cookbook that packages a skill (domain instructions), connectors (governed data access), and sub-agents (focused Claude models for sub-tasks). The same pattern applies to any vertical — swap the skill markdown and connector list for your domain.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers building workflows that run longer than a single API round-trip: document processing pipelines, multi-step research agents, KYC or compliance screening, month-end close automation. Particularly useful for teams on paid Claude plans who want Anthropic-managed infrastructure rather than self-hosted orchestration, and for anyone who wants to use the pre-built financial-services cookbooks as a starting point.
pros: Durable session state — no external database needed to persist agent context across steps
Task budgets in public beta give explicit token spend control for cost-sensitive production runs
Ready-to-fork cookbooks for 10 financial workflows available immediately at the financial services marketplace
Available on all paid Claude plans; works via the claude-opus-4-7 API model identifier
cons: Still in public beta — session limits, pricing at scale, and SLAs are not fully documented yet
Best model (Opus 4.7) is $5/$25 per million tokens in/out — long agentic runs get expensive fast without task budgets
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Anthropic API key on a paid plan
- `anthropic` Python SDK >= 0.30 (for Managed Agents support)
- Python 3.11+

## Step 1 — Install the SDK

```bash
pip install --upgrade anthropic
```

## Step 2 — Create a managed agent session

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()  # Reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env

# Start a durable agent session
session = client.beta.managed_agents.sessions.create(
    model="claude-opus-4-7",
    system="You are a financial analyst. Follow the KYC screening workflow in the attached skill.",
    tools=[{"type": "computer_20250124", "name": "computer", "display_width_px": 1024, "display_height_px": 768}],
    # Task budget caps total tokens across the run
    task_budget={"max_tokens": 200000},
    betas=["managed-agents-2026-05"]
)

print(f"Session ID: {session.id}")
```

## Step 3 — Send work to the session

```python
# Submit a task into the running session
result = client.beta.managed_agents.sessions.run(
    session_id=session.id,
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Screen the attached onboarding record for KYC/AML compliance. Output a risk rating and flag any document gaps."
        }
    ]
)

for block in result.content:
    print(block.text)
```

## Step 4 — Use a pre-built financial cookbook (optional)

```bash
# Clone the financial-services cookbook repo
git clone https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services
cd financial-services/kyc-screener

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run the KYC screener cookbook
python run_agent.py --input ./sample_onboarding_record.json
```

## Gotcha
The `betas=["managed-agents-2026-05"]` header is mandatory — requests without it fall back to stateless inference and lose session persistence. The beta header name will change on GA; watch the Anthropic changelog at `releasebot.io/updates/anthropic` for the update.

learn.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: OpenAI's open-source terminal coding agent with plugin marketplace, /goal workflows, and AWS Bedrock support.

detail.whatItDoes:
The Codex CLI is an open-source agentic coding assistant that runs in the terminal and drives file edits, shell commands, and test execution autonomously. This week's release adds persisted /goal workflows (create a goal, pause and resume it across sessions), a plugin marketplace (install from GitHub, git URLs, or local directories), configurable TUI keymaps, Ctrl+R reverse search in prompt history, and first-class Amazon Bedrock support with AWS SigV4 signing.

Permission profiles have been overhauled: the deprecated --full-auto flag is gone, replaced by named profiles (sandboxed, network-restricted, etc.) that can be set per project in codex.toml. MCP server support is now comprehensive — namespaced registration, parallel-call opt-in, and sandbox-state metadata.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers who prefer terminal-first workflows over GUI coding assistants. Particularly useful for teams using Symphony (the Codex orchestration spec released last week) — Symphony is built on the Codex App Server, so staying current on the CLI is a prerequisite. AWS-native teams can now route Codex through Bedrock and apply usage toward existing AWS commitments.
pros: Open-source (Apache 2.0) with an active changelog and Elixir/Python/TypeScript SDK surface
AWS Bedrock support: authenticate with AWS credentials, bill to your AWS account, keep data in your VPC
Plugin marketplace means the community can extend Codex without forking the core
Persisted /goal workflows survive terminal restarts — critical for multi-hour agentic tasks
cons: --full-auto is deprecated with no grace period in some versions; old automation scripts will break
Plugin marketplace vetting is still community-driven — review plugin code before installing in sensitive repos
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node 20+
- macOS or Linux (Windows supported but some sandbox features require WSL2)
- OpenAI API key with Codex access, or AWS credentials for Bedrock routing

## Step 1 — Install

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex
codex --version
```

## Step 2 — Configure (OpenAI direct)

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

Create `~/.config/codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[defaults]
model = "gpt-5.5"
trust_level = "sandboxed"   # replaces deprecated --full-auto
reasoning_effort = "high"   # options: low, medium, high, xhigh
```

## Step 2 (alt) — Configure for AWS Bedrock

```bash
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
```

```toml
[provider]
type = "bedrock"
model = "openai.gpt-5-5"    # Bedrock model ID
region = "us-east-1"
```

## Step 3 — Run your first task

```bash
# One-shot task
codex exec "Add input validation to the user registration endpoint and write a test for the new edge cases"

# Interactive TUI
codex
```

## Step 4 — Create a persistent goal

Inside the Codex TUI:

```
/goal create "Refactor the authentication module to use the new JWT library"
# Codex assigns the goal an ID and begins working
# You can /goal pause <id> and /goal resume <id> across sessions
```

## Step 5 — Install a marketplace plugin

```bash
codex marketplace add https://github.com/example/codex-plugin-linear
```

## Gotcha
If you were using `--full-auto` in CI scripts, replace it with `--trust sandboxed` or `--trust network-restricted` before upgrading. The flag was removed in recent releases and causes a startup error, not a deprecation warning.
